chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"When you see the elder narrating on Friday in the mosque from the stories of the pre-Islamic era of ignorance, throw his head, even with pebbles."

key_terms.أَحَادِيثُ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: Stories of the pre-Islamic era of ignorance

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when scholars throw pebbles at an elder's head in the mosque?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarly tradition, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the importance of maintaining the sanctity of Friday sermons by avoiding *ahadith al-Jahiliyyah*—pre-Islamic tales of entertainment or triviality that distract from spiritual reflection. The instruction to 'throw his head' with pebbles is interpreted not merely as physical correction but as a symbolic act of censure (*ta'zir*) to remind the narrator of his duty to the community. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on distinguishing between beneficial religious knowledge and mere worldly storytelling during sacred gatherings.
